sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A Kickstarter plan: a sovereign website on a configured Android tablet or Raspberry Pis, three tiers.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: An appliance on Kickstarter, Android first, three tiers, backer's choice, the UK first, launch alone.

sections.label: The product
sections.line: A tablet configured with the site, editing, monitoring, an AI app and a vault backup, or Raspberry Pis.

sections.label: Android, and why not an iPad first
sections.line: Android is open and fully ours; the Web Summit tablet is the prototype; iOS a stretch goal.

sections.label: The tiers
sections.line: £50 supporter; £500 with about £250 of hardware; £1,000 with about £500; add-ons.

sections.label: What £250 and £500 buy today
sections.line: Lenovo Idea Tab £209.99, Galaxy Tab S10 FE £509, the Volla Tablet with /e/OS, Pi 5 kits from £99.70.

sections.label: A website served from home
sections.line: Pis as hosts alongside GitHub Pages, reached without proprietary tunnels where possible.

sections.label: The goal and the stretch goals
sections.line: The UK as the base goal, Portugal first, then countries by vote, and iOS; all-or-nothing.

sections.label: Value first
sections.line: Every backer sees their own site in a vault before anything ships.

sections.label: Launch alone, partner later
sections.line: Launch with Android and open source, then talk to device makers as a funded project.

sections.label: After the campaign
sections.line: Late pledges, pre-orders on sovereignwebsite.ai, and Patreon later.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nothing submitted; prices are examples; the device software is a plan; no goal amount yet.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The afternoon's record and UK retailers' pages on 19 November.
